record.paper_title: The 1999 Heineman Prize Address Integrable models in statistical mechanics: The hidden field with unsolved problems
record.original_question: Does the susceptibility of the isotropic two-dimensional Ising model possess a natural boundary on the complex-temperature unit circle |v| = 1 because the singularities contributed by successive n-particle terms become dense there, and if so, how does that analyticity structure distinguish integrable models from generic non-integrable models?

evidence.quote: There is one final problem of the hidden field of integrable models which I want to discuss. Namely the question of what is the relation of an integrable model to a generic physical system which does not satisfy a Yang-Baxter equation.

However Nickel goes far beyond this scaling and for the isotropic case where Ev = Eh = E in term of the variable v = sinh 2E/kT he shows that succes�sive terms in the series contribute singularities that eventually become dense on the unit circle in the complex plane |v| = 1.
The proof of Nickel’s conjecture will, if correct, open up a new view on what it means to be integrable.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the isotropic two-dimensional Ising model on the square lattice with equal horizontal and vertical nearest-neighbor couplings E_h = E_v = E and inverse temperature 1/(kT). Introduce the variable
   v = sinh(2E/(kT)).
The zero-field magnetic susceptibility χ(v) admits, in the high-temperature regime, an expansion
   χ(v) = Σ_{n odd} χ^{(n)}(v)
into n-particle contributions χ^{(n)}(v), each given by an n-fold integral that is analytic in a neighborhood of v = 0 and extends meromorphically with a known finite set of algebraic/logarithmic singularities accumulating on the curve |v| = 1 as n → ∞. (A similar decomposition holds in the low-temperature regime with even n.)

Question:
(a) Prove or disprove that χ(v), viewed as a function of the complex variable v, possesses the unit circle |v| = 1 as a natural boundary, i.e. that χ(v) cannot be analytically continued across any arc of |v| = 1, because the singularities contributed by the successive n-particle terms become dense on |v| = 1 and no global cancellation removes them.

(b) Assuming (a) holds, formulate and justify a precise sense in which the presence of such a natural boundary in the susceptibility of a lattice model is a hallmark of Yang–Baxter integrability: namely, show that a generic non-integrable two-dimensional lattice spin model with short-range interactions does not exhibit such a dense accumulation of n-particle singularities on a one-dimensional curve in the complex temperature plane, so that its susceptibility extends analytically across that curve.
artifact.status_search_result: The Nickel conjecture that the susceptibility of the isotropic 2D Ising model has a natural boundary on |v| = 1 (equivalently |k| = 1 in modular variables) remains open. Subsequent works by Nickel, Guttmann, Boukraa, Hassani, Maillard, Zenine and others provide strong numerical and structural evidence (power-spectrum analyses, n-fold-integral singularity studies, diagonal-susceptibility results) supporting the conjecture, but no rigorous proof is known. The deeper claim that such a natural boundary distinguishes integrable from generic non-integrable models is likewise unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Analyticity of the Ising susceptibility: An interpretation
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses the conjectured natural boundary of the full susceptibility on |v|=1 and the mechanism by which singularities of n-particle contributions accumulate there.
status_evidence.claim: The natural-boundary conjecture is still being investigated and supported by analytic/numerical evidence rather than proved.

status_evidence.title: On the diagonal susceptibility of the 2D Ising model
status_evidence.snippet: Establishes properties of the diagonal susceptibility and discusses the unit circle as a natural boundary for that restricted object.
status_evidence.claim: Rigorous results are obtained for the diagonal susceptibility, but the full-susceptibility conjecture remains open.

status_evidence.title: Experimental mathematics on the magnetic susceptibility of the square lattice Ising model
status_evidence.snippet: Large-scale series analyses giving strong evidence for a dense set of singularities on |s|=1 in the susceptibility.
status_evidence.claim: Strong numerical evidence for, but not a proof of, Nickel's natural-boundary conjecture.

status_evidence.title: The susceptibility of the square lattice Ising model: New developments
status_evidence.snippet: Reviews structure of n-particle contributions and their accumulating singularities on the unit circle.
status_evidence.claim: Treats the natural-boundary statement as a conjecture supported by extensive computation.
